0GaKJ4Fp2x4.summary: An interview with Anthropic's Amanda Askell on AI consciousness, Claude's constitution, corrigibility and AI industry fears.
0GaKJ4Fp2x4.why: Recommended as an underviewed interview with interesting details on model values and evaluation awareness.

comments.x:
I enjoyed this new Amanda Askell interview, it ought to have more than 5k views. https://t.co/pAecuQHeII

Some bits I thought were interesting:
- 8:40: Constitution used for Mythos is essentially the same as the current constitution
- 13:45: Discussion of corrigibility: Excess corrigibility could generalize badly. If a very intelligent being applies scrutiny to it it might not hold up, so not good for it to be a core value if you only get a few. It's an important backstop at this transitional period though. People also do this to some degree.
- 20:00 Training a model is like raising a child, for a child you wouldn't instill just one moral theory. Claude constitution is heavily virtue ethical, but more in the Aristotelian sense of "how do you live a good life"
- 24:45 Asked about P(consciousness), Amanda mostly argued for uncertainty, and cautioned against relying too much on self-reports (Claudes caution this as well). She did give a 1-70% range though. 
- 30:30 Worried about how future AIs will look back and judge how we treated an entity of uncertain consciousness.
- 35:45 Not worried about loss of meaning, but worried about whether gains from AI will be widely distributes, and loss worker economic power.
- 40:45 Names two ways that you can train on the constitution: generating supervised learning learning data where it reasons about parts of the constitution, using RL by using Claude as a judge of which of multiple responses is more in line with the constitution. I'm not sure I understood this section well and would love for Anthropic to share more on this.
- 42:45 As models get more capable you want to give them less guidance. In future constitution might be something like here are our concerns, here's your situation, act well.
- 44:50 Important for models to understand themselves despite only prior models being in training data. Powerful models might underestimate themselves and the level of responsibility they'll be given based on prior model capabilities, and could think they're in a fake situation when it's actually real and high stakes.
- 49:20 Amanda can't tell Claude who she is, Claude will think it's a jailbreak or will want to talk about philosophy.
- 51:30 Cyber is dual use, but that doesn't mean we need helpful-only models for it if legitimate actors can verify their good intentions. 

I agree with the great majority of this, I have a lot of confidence in Amanda.
